title: Access governance packaging experiment: contract obligations and price levers for identity controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Define and validate packaging and contract commitments for identity and access governance features (SSO integrations, SAML, federated login flows, and role-based access controls) so Sales has a clear playbook and Legal has bounded obligations.

Background: Enterprise customers increasingly request identity guarantees in contracts (time-to-revoke, audit logs, role isolation) and treat RBAC/SSO as a gating feature. We currently have informal pricing add-ons and engineering support offers; this experiment aims to formalize: (a) which identity controls are included in base vs. paid tiers, (b) the minimum contractual commitments we will promise (e.g., support for SAML 2.0, up to N IdPs, SSO onboarding SLA), and (c) test price sensitivity and negotiation outcomes across ARR bands.

Scope: Pricing experiments and contract template language for: SAML-based SSO, OIDC support, seat/role-level RBAC, audit log retention for identity events, and expedited SSO onboarding (paid). Out of scope: full on-prem packaging of identity infrastructure, custom IdP integrations that require engineering projects (those will remain professional services).
acceptance_criteria: Clear binary packaging decision matrix that maps features to tiers (self-serve free, growth, enterprise)
Contract clause text for identity commitments accepted by Legal as a template (no open engineering deliverables left unspecified)
At least 3 pricing experiments defined (A/B or sales playbook variations) with measurement plan and target sample sizes
Sales playbook and objection-handling doc created and shared with AE pilots
Engineering feasibility doc with estimated effort and rollout plan for the smallest required product work
success_metrics: Conversion lift: +5% win-rate on RFPs mentioning SSO/RBAC in AE pilot cohort
Time-to-close reduction: -10% median deal cycle for deals requiring identity commitments
Price capture: >$Xk average uplift on enterprise deals that elect paid onboarding or RBAC add-ons (baseline to be defined)
Support load: no more than 15% increase in onboarding tickets for SSO in first 3 months post-launch
notes: 2025-01-12 Aisha Patel: Kickoff — scoped requirements, validated ask frequency with Sales Ops. Requesting Legal and Applied ML (for audit/telemetry needs) to join discovery.

2025-01-14 Marco Li: Collected Sales feedback from 7 AE interviews — common asks: guaranteed SSO onboarding window (7 business days), RBAC role export, and audit trail retention options (30/90/365 days).
2025-01-16 Legal (Heather Nguyen): Initial redlines — cannot commit to unlimited IdP integrations; propose limit to 3 IdPs per tenant in contract with add-on pricing for more.

2025-01-17 Eng (Sreena Rao): High-level implementation notes — SSO onboarding SLA requires a lightweight onboarding flow, templates for IdP metadata exchange, and a visibility dashboard. Estimated lift for baseline support: 3 sprint-equivalents across runtime and console teams.

2025-01-18 Pricing (Jon Park): Proposed two-lever pricing experiment: 1) include SSO and basic RBAC in Enterprise package at no extra fee vs. 2) charge a fixed onboarding fee + monthly per-seat RBAC premium. Need to simulate ROI on historical pipeline.
2025-01-20 PM update: Preparing experiment artifacts and AE pilot list (10 target customers across fintech, health, and SaaS). Legal to review final clause text by 2025-01-24.
